question:
**Case Study 4: Business – Inventory and Profit Analysis**

A company sells two products, X and Y. Over three months, the number of units sold is recorded as the matrix $S = \begin{bmatrix} 120 & 100 \\ 150 & 130 \\ 170 & 160 \end{bmatrix}$, where columns correspond to X and Y, and rows are months 1, 2, 3. The profit per item is given as column vector $P = \begin{bmatrix} 20 \\ 30 \end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Find the profit for each month as a column vector $Q = S P$.
(b) If the company wants to increase the profit per item by 10% next quarter, write the appropriate profit vector and calculate the new total profit for all three months.
(c) If the sales matrix $S$ is replaced with its transpose, explain the mathematical and practical effect for profit calculation.
explanation:
(a) $Q = S P = \begin{bmatrix} 120 & 100 \\ 150 & 130 \\ 170 & 160 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 20 \\ 30 \end{bmatrix}$

For Month 1: $120 \times 20 + 100 \times 30 = 2400 + 3000 = 5400$

For Month 2: $150 \times 20 + 130 \times 30 = 3000 + 3900 = 6900$

For Month 3: $170 \times 20 + 160 \times 30 = 3400 + 4800 = 8200$

$Q = \begin{bmatrix} 5400 \\ 6900 \\ 8200 \end{bmatrix}$

(b) New profit per item: 10% more

$20 \times 1.1 = 22$, $30 \times 1.1 = 33$

New profit vector: $P' = \begin{bmatrix} 22 \\ 33 \end{bmatrix}$

Total profit: $Q' = S P'$

Month 1: $120 \times 22 + 100 \times 33 = 2640 + 3300 = 5940$

Month 2: $150 \times 22 + 130 \times 33 = 3300 + 4290 = 7590$

Month 3: $170 \times 22 + 160 \times 33 = 3740 + 5280 = 9020$

Total profit (all months): $5940 + 7590 + 9020 = 22,550$

(c) $S^T$ is $2 \times 3$ instead of $3 \times 2$. If $P$ is $2 \times 1$, $S^T P$ is not defined ($2 \times 3$ by $2 \times 1$), so the multiplication is not possible. Thus, transposing $S$ destroys the interpretation of 'profit per month'. Mathematically, $S^T$ can only be multiplied from the right by a $3 \times 1$ column vector (e.g., if profit is given per month, not per product).

options.A:
(a) $Q=SP=\begin{bmatrix}5400\\6900\\8200\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) New profit vector $P'=\begin{bmatrix}22\\33\end{bmatrix}$ and new total profit for all three months is $22550$.
(c) $S^TP$ is not defined because $S^T$ is $2\times3$ and $P$ is $2\times1$, so the profit-per-month interpretation is lost.
options.B:
(a) $Q=\begin{bmatrix}5400&6900&8200\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) New profit vector $P'=\begin{bmatrix}20\\30\end{bmatrix}$ and total profit is $20500$.
(c) $S^TP$ gives the same monthly profit vector.
options.C:
(a) $Q=\begin{bmatrix}220\\280\\330\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) New total profit is $9020$.
(c) Transpose does not affect multiplication order.
options.D:
(a) $Q=\begin{bmatrix}5400\\6900\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) New profit vector is $\begin{bmatrix}30\\20\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) $S^TP$ is always defined and gives product-wise profit.
